title: quant-sensitivity-grid-4bit-int8-fp8-proto
content:
Purpose:
Small working spreadsheet + decision grid to help PM/Eng pick quantization target for a model family given an SLA (p99 latency), cost target ($/1M tokens), and tolerable quality delta (relative to FP16). This is a proto that we should convert to a proper Optimize UI recommendation later.

Context + assumptions:
- Models evaluated: Llama-2-70B (base FP16), Mistral-7B-large equivalent family (for smaller models), and a Redwood-verified 30B candidate (internal name: red-30b).
- Hardware reference: H100-80GB for peak perf (hosted), A100-40GB for Dedicated baseline, and L4 for low-cost inference.
- Eval set: 8k dev prompts from product-safety + question-answering + summarization mixes (sampled from confluence:Quant-evals-2025). Quality metric: EM/Exact-match for QA, ROUGE-L for summarization, + human pass-rate proxy for safety prompts.
- Baseline is FP16 numbers we measured in perf runs on H100.

How to use this sheet:
- Row per model-variant; columns are measured/estimated deltas for quant modes (INT8, FP8, 4-bit).
- Cost estimates convert GPU-hours -> $/1M tokens using our internal pricing table (see linked jira:OPT-512).
- Use the sensitivity score (0..1) to prioritize safe targets: 1 == no quality regression, 0 == unacceptable regression.

Quick executive summary (proto):
- INT8: generally safe for 7B and 30B families with <1% quality delta on typical evals; for 70B we see 0.5-2% delta depending on layerwise scales and per-channel calibration. Latency: +-5% net. Memory: ~2x reduction (KV+weights). Cost: ~30-40% reduction in $/1M tokens on A100/H100 when batching moderately (batch size 8-32).
- FP8: best win for 30B/70B on memory w/ little extra engineering; quality delta similar to INT8 for many workloads but requires updated kernels. Latency often slightly better than INT8 due to smaller compute but depends on GPU TFN support. Cost: ~35-45% reduction.
- 4-bit (QLoRA/LLM-int4 style): largest memory win (~3-4x) and biggest cost reduction (~55-65%), but quality regression variable: 1-6% on standard QA/summarization; for safety-critical workloads this may be unacceptable without post-calibration or small distillation. Latency: can improve raw token throughput but KV/cache overheads sometimes increase p99 if packing not tuned.

Example sensitivity/grid (CSV-style rows you can paste into a sheet):
Model,Hardware,Baseline_tokens_per_sec,Baseline_cost_per_1M_tokens_USD,Mode,Quality_delta_pct,Latency_p99_change_pct,Memory_reduction_pct,Estimated_cost_per_1M_tokens_USD,Sensitivity_score,Notes
Llama-2-70B,H100,3200,1200,INT8,0.8,5,50,780,0.86,"per-channel calibrate; rebuild kv-caching kernel"
Llama-2-70B,H100,3200,1200,FP8,0.6,3,55,690,0.91,"FP8 kernels stable on H100; need quant-aware layernorm fixes"
Llama-2-70B,A100,2100,1500,4-bit,2.7,8,75,560,0.62,"good for batch offline; p99 spikes in small-batch chat routes"
Red-30B,A100,4800,420,INT8,0.4,2,48,260,0.94,"low regression, recommend pilot on Dedicated"
Red-30B,L4,5200,300,4-bit,1.9,0,70,110,0.75,"cost-effective for high-traffic read-only endpoints"
Mistral-7B,H100,9800,90,INT8,0.1,1,45,50,0.98,"safe default for chat-style apps"

Spreadsheet formulas (copy to Excel/Sheets):
- Estimated_cost_per_1M_tokens_USD = Baseline_cost_per_1M_tokens_USD * (1 - Memory_reduction_pct/100 * 0.8)
  (explanation: we assume token cost scales roughly with memory reduction times 80% because some costs are fixed e.g. orchestration/noise)
- Sensitivity_score = MAX(0, 1 - (Quality_delta_pct / Quality_tolerance_pct)) where Quality_tolerance_pct is an input cell (default 2%)

Decision heuristics (proto rules to convert to recommendations in Optimize):
- If Sensitivity_score >= 0.9 and Estimated_cost_reduction >= 30% -> Recommend: "Enable quant mode (auto)" with canary = 5% traffic, monitor metrics: rouge/qa-EM, p99 latency, model-fallback-rate.
- If 0.6 <= Sensitivity_score < 0.9 -> Recommend: "Pilot (A/B) with eval prompts" + automated rollback if QA_EM drops > Quality_tolerance_pct or error-rate increases > 0.5%.
- If Sensitivity_score < 0.6 -> Recommend: "Do not quantize in production; explore post-training calibration or small distillation".

Engineering checklist for experiment runs:
- [ ] Add per-channel calibration step (script path: github:infra/quant-kernels#234)
- [ ] Run perf harness on H100 + A100 for p50/p95/p99 (scripts in repo infra/perf/harness)
- [ ] Compute cost conversion using dedicated pricing sheet (linked jira:OPT-512)
- [ ] Create canary rollout config in console (route: product/checkout/chat -> quant-30b-int8)
- [ ] Add regression alerts in Optimize: dataset ids (confluence:Quant-evals-2025 -> dataset:qa-8k)

Open questions / experiments to prioritize:
- How much of the 4-bit quality gap can be closed with 1-2 epochs of targeted distillation on the product QA eval set? (small experiment: red-30b-int4-distill-1e)
- FP8 runtime stability across Dedicated GPUs (A100 vs H100) — need matrix testing across kernels.
- Can we automate per-customer routing: low-cost quantized for read-only embeddings/semantic search but FP16 for write/safety-sensitive calls? (policy: route-by-intent)

Notes from earlier runs (raw):
- Observed a 0.5% QA EM drop on 70B INT8 when using naive min-max quant; switching to per-channel symmetric scale reduced that to ~0.2%.
- 4-bit on L4 showed large cost wins but unpredictable p99 tail for very small batch sizes; likely due to kernel launch overhead + cache warming.

Next steps (owners):
- Marco: run A100 full-batch sweep for red-30b INT8/FP8 and push perf logs to confluence:Quant-evals-2025 by 2025-03-10.
- Priya: build Optimize recommendation UI skeleton for "quant-recommendation" and wire sensitivity_score input by 2025-03-20.
- Aisha: consolidate cost conversion table and finalize decision thresholds with PM on 2025-03-05.

Todo / TODOs:
- Add small section mapping to billing product units (tokens->calls) so PMs can present customer-facing savings.
- Validate costs on lower-tier Dedicated SKUs and with burst capacity.

Appendix: shorthand for columns used in the sheet (so non-data folk can read it):
- Baseline_tokens_per_sec: measured average throughput at batch size X (document batch sizes in a separate column in the real sheet).
- Baseline_cost_per_1M_tokens_USD: internal conversion (GPU hour cost / tokens-per-hour * 1e6).
- Memory_reduction_pct: (baseline_mem - quant_mem) / baseline_mem * 100.
- Quality_delta_pct: positive means worse than baseline (higher loss or lower metric).

Comments: this file is intentionally informal — it's a working proto to converge on a repeatable sensitivity grid. Move to a canonical sheet in shared_drives/product/optimize/ when we lock thresholds.
